title: Detection and quantification of the giant protein titin by SDS-agarose gel electrophoresis
author: Zhu, Guo
materials: Bromophenol blue was added and stirred till dissolved. The final volume was brought up by adding deionized water, and filtered through a Millex HA 0.45 or 0.22 μm filter (Millipore) to remove any fine particulate materiel. The filtered buffer was aliquoted into 1 mL or 2 mL microfuge vials, and stored at −20 °C for future use.

steps.title: Prepare SDS‑agarose sample buffer
steps.instruction: Make a buffer containing 8 M urea, 2 M thiourea, 30 % glycerol, 3 % SDS (w/v), 75 mM DTT, 0.03 % bromophenol blue and 0.05 M Tris–HCl pH 6.8.

substeps.instruction: Add urea and thiourea to a clean beaker, dissolve in glycerol.
Add 10 % (v/v) deionized water to speed dissolution; stir on a hot plate at ≤40 °C until clear at room temperature.
Add 10 % (w/v) mixed‑bed resin (Fisher Rexyn 300 or Bio‑Rad AG 501‑X8) to deionize; stir 15 min at room temperature.
If a conductivity meter is available, confirm conductivity <5 µmhos.
Filter the mixture through filter paper to remove resin.
Add Tris‑base and SDS; adjust pH to 7.5 with HCl.
Add solid DTT, stir until dissolved; continuously readjust pH down to 6.8.
Add bromophenol blue, stir until dissolved.
Bring the solution to the final volume with deionized water.
Filter through a Millex HA 0.45 µm or 0.22 µm filter to remove fine particles.
Aliquot into 1 mL or 2 mL micro‑fuge tubes and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Extract protein from cardiac tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize frozen cardiac tissue in the prepared sample buffer and recover soluble protein.

substeps.instruction: Dissect cardiac tissue from WT, HT and HM rats and flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen.
Weigh 10–15 mg tissue per 1 mL of sample buffer; add protease inhibitors.
Homogenize on ice (0 °C) with a Dounce homogenizer.
Transfer homogenate to a 1.5 mL tube and heat at 60 °C for 10 min.
Centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 2 min; collect the supernatant.
Use supernatant immediately for loading or store at –80 °C.
For silver staining, dilute the sample 1:5 or 1:10.

steps.title: Create acrylamide plug
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 cm high acrylamide plug to anchor the agarose gel.

substeps.instruction: Mix in a beaker: 1.924 mL deionized water, 1.7 mL 50 % glycerol, 2.12 mL 3 M Tris (pH 9.3), 2.72 mL 40 % acrylamide, 24 µL 10 % APS, and 13 µL TEMED.
Add 2.5 mL of this plug solution to each gel assembly.
Add a small amount of water or ethanol on top of the plug to even the surface and aid polymerization.
Allow polymerization for 20–30 min.
Invert the gel unit and blot off excess liquid with paper towels.

steps.title: Prepare and melt agarose resolving gel
steps.instruction: Make the 1 % agarose resolving gel solution and keep it hot for casting.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑heat the assembled gel plates in an oven at >60 °C and <80 °C for ~30 min.
Weigh 0.8 g Sea Kem Gold agarose and place in a 500 mL beaker.

In a 100 mL graduated cylinder combine 48 mL 50 % glycerol, 16 mL 5× electrophoresis buffer (0.25 M Tris‑base, 1.92 M glycine, 0.5 % SDS, pH 8.5, no adjustment needed), then add deionized water to a final volume of 80 mL.
Mix the buffer‑glycerol solution well and pour into the beaker with agarose; swirl to combine.
Cover the beaker with plastic wrap, poke a few holes, and microwave for ~3 min, stopping intermittently to release bubbles, until the mixture boils and agarose is fully dissolved.

steps.title: Cast agarose gel and insert comb
steps.instruction: Pour the hot agarose solution into the gel plates, set the comb, and allow the gel to solidify.

substeps.instruction: Remove the pre‑warmed gel assembly from the oven.
Immediately pour ~40 mL of the hot agarose solution into the plates (directly or via a pre‑warmed 10 mL syringe).
Insert a 1.5 mm thick, 20‑lane comb on top of the gel.
Let the gel cool and solidify for 30–45 min at room temperature or a shorter time at 4 °C.
Gels may be used immediately or stored overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Run SDS‑agarose electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load protein samples into the gel wells and run the vertical SDS‑agarose electrophoresis system for 3 hours.

steps.title: Fix gels post‑run
steps.instruction: Remove gels from the apparatus, fix proteins, and prepare for staining.

substeps.instruction: Disassemble the gel plates, discard the wells and acrylamide plug, and cut the gel with a spacer; cut a small corner to mark lane order.
Fix each gel in 500 mL of 50 % methanol, 12 % glacial acetic acid and 5 % (w/v) glycerol for at least 1 h (up to 2 days) with gentle shaking in a sealed polypropylene container.
Rinse the polypropylene containers with concentrated nitric acid before reuse to remove precipitated silver.
Remove the fixing solution and dry the gels overnight in a 37 °C incubator.

steps.title: Dry gels overnight
steps.instruction: Place the fixed gels in a 37 °C incubator and dry them overnight to improve band sharpness and reduce background.

steps.title: Silver stain agarose gels
steps.instruction: Perform silver staining on the dried gels to visualize titin isoforms.

substeps.instruction: Wash each gel 3 times with deionized water, 15 min per wash.
Wash in 20 g/L potassium ferrocyanide solution for 5 min.
Wash again 3 times with deionized water, 5 min each.
Prepare Solution A: dissolve 25 g sodium carbonate in 500 mL deionized water (in a 1 L beaker).
Prepare Solution B: dissolve 1 g silver nitrate, 1 g ammonium nitrate, 5 g tungstosilicic acid and add 3 mL 37 % formaldehyde to 500 mL deionized water.
Just before staining, slowly add Solution B to stirring Solution A.
Shake gels in the staining solution until bands appear (5–10 min); monitor closely to avoid over‑staining.
Decant staining solution and add 500 mL of 1 % (v/v) acetic acid; shake 5 min to stop staining.
Decant the acid and wash gels with deionized water for 5 min.
Dry gels between two sheets of cellophane paper (RPI #1080) with several drops of glycerol for one day.
